nodes.name: Axiom
nodes.desc: Axiom is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that has targeted the aerospace, defense, government, manufacturing, and media sectors since at least 2008.

nodes.name: Moafee
nodes.desc: Moafee is a threat group that appears to operate from the Guandong Province of China.

nodes.name: Cleaver
nodes.desc: Cleaver is a threat group that has been attributed to Iranian actors and is responsible for activity tracked as Operation Cleaver.

nodes.name: Ke3chang
nodes.desc: Ke3chang is a threat group attributed to actors operating out of China.

nodes.name: APT12
nodes.desc: APT12 is a threat group that has been attributed to China.

nodes.name: APT1
nodes.desc: APT1 is a Chinese threat group that has been attributed to the 2nd Bureau of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) General Staff Department’s (GSD) 3rd Department, commonly known by its Military Unit Cover Designator (MUCD) as Unit 61398.

nodes.name: APT28
nodes.aliases: IRON TWILIGHT;SNAKEMACKEREL;Swallowtail;Group 74;Sednit;Sofacy;Pawn Storm;Fancy Bear;STRONTIUM;Tsar Team;Threat Group-4127;TG-4127;Forest Blizzard;FROZENLAKE;GruesomeLarch
nodes.desc: APT28 is a threat group that has been attributed to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 85th Main Special Service Center (GTsSS) military unit 26165.

nodes.name: Carbanak
nodes.desc: Carbanak is a cybercriminal group that has used Carbanak malware to target financial institutions since at least 2013.

nodes.name: Deep Panda
nodes.desc: Deep Panda is a suspected Chinese threat group known to target many industries, including government, defense, financial, and telecommunications.

nodes.name: Turla
nodes.desc: Turla is a cyber espionage threat group that has been attributed to Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB).

nodes.name: PittyTiger
nodes.desc: PittyTiger is a threat group believed to operate out of China that uses multiple different types of malware to maintain command and control.

nodes.name: Darkhotel
nodes.desc: Darkhotel is a suspected South Korean threat group that has targeted victims primarily in East Asia since at least 2004.

nodes.name: APT30
nodes.desc: APT30 is a threat group suspected to be associated with the Chinese government.

nodes.name: APT29
nodes.aliases: IRON RITUAL;IRON HEMLOCK;NobleBaron;Dark Halo;NOBELIUM;UNC2452;YTTRIUM;The Dukes;Cozy Bear;CozyDuke;SolarStorm;Blue Kitsune;UNC3524;Midnight Blizzard
nodes.desc: APT29 is threat group that has been attributed to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR).

nodes.name: admin@338
nodes.desc: admin@338 is a China-based cyber threat group.

nodes.name: Naikon
nodes.desc: Naikon is assessed to be a state-sponsored cyber espionage group attributed to the Chinese People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) Chengdu Military Region Second Technical Reconnaissance Bureau (Military Unit Cover Designator 78020).

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.desc: Equation is a sophisticated threat group that employs multiple remote access tools.

nodes.name: Molerats
nodes.desc: Molerats is an Arabic-speaking, politically-motivated threat group that has been operating since 2012.

nodes.name: APT3
nodes.desc: APT3 is a China-based threat group that researchers have attributed to China's Ministry of State Security.

nodes.name: APT16
nodes.desc: APT16 is a China-based threat group that has launched spearphishing campaigns targeting Japanese and Taiwanese organizations.

nodes.name: Putter Panda
nodes.desc: Putter Panda is a Chinese threat group that has been attributed to Unit 61486 of the 12th Bureau of the PLA’s 3rd General Staff Department (GSD).

nodes.name: APT17
nodes.desc: APT17 is a China-based threat group that has conducted network intrusions against U.S.

nodes.name: APT18
nodes.desc: APT18 is a threat group that has operated since at least 2009 and has targeted a range of industries, including technology, manufacturing, human rights groups, government, and medical.

nodes.name: Threat Group-3390
nodes.aliases: Earth Smilodon;TG-3390;Emissary Panda;BRONZE UNION;APT27;Iron Tiger;LuckyMouse;Linen Typhoon
nodes.desc: Threat Group-3390 is a Chinese threat group that has extensively used strategic Web compromises to target victims.

nodes.name: Threat Group-1314
nodes.desc: Threat Group-1314 is an unattributed threat group that has used compromised credentials to log into a victim's remote access infrastructure.

nodes.name: Scarlet Mimic
nodes.desc: Scarlet Mimic is a threat group that has targeted minority rights activists.

nodes.name: Lotus Blossom
nodes.desc: Lotus Blossom is a long-standing threat group largely targeting various entities in Asia since at least 2009.

nodes.name: Lazarus Group
nodes.aliases: Labyrinth Chollima;HIDDEN COBRA;Guardians of Peace;ZINC;NICKEL ACADEMY;Diamond Sleet
nodes.desc: Lazarus Group is a North Korean state-sponsored cyber threat group attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB).

nodes.name: Poseidon Group
nodes.desc: Poseidon Group is a Portuguese-speaking threat group that has been active since at least 2005.

nodes.name: Sandworm Team
nodes.desc: Sandworm Team is a destructive threat group that has been attributed to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) Main Center for Special Technologies (GTsST) military unit 74455.

nodes.name: Dragonfly
nodes.aliases: TEMP.Isotope;DYMALLOY;Berserk Bear;TG-4192;Crouching Yeti;IRON LIBERTY;Energetic Bear;Ghost Blizzard;BROMINE
nodes.desc: Dragonfly is a cyber espionage group that has been attributed to Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) Center 16.

nodes.name: GCMAN
nodes.desc: GCMAN is a threat group that focuses on targeting banks for the purpose of transferring money to e-currency services.

nodes.name: FIN6
nodes.desc: FIN6 is a cyber crime group that has stolen payment card data and sold it for profit on underground marketplaces.

nodes.name: Stealth Falcon
nodes.desc: Stealth Falcon is a threat group that has conducted targeted spyware attacks against Emirati journalists, activists, and dissidents since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Suckfly
nodes.desc: Suckfly is a China-based threat group that has been active since at least 2014.

nodes.name: Patchwork
nodes.desc: Patchwork is a cyber espionage group that was first observed in December 2015.

nodes.name: Strider
nodes.desc: Strider is a threat group that has been active since at least 2011 and has targeted victims in Russia, China, Sweden, Belgium, Iran, and Rwanda.

nodes.name: Group5
nodes.desc: Group5 is a threat group with a suspected Iranian nexus, though this attribution is not definite.

nodes.name: Winnti Group
nodes.desc: Winnti Group is a threat group with Chinese origins that has been active since at least 2010.

nodes.name: menuPass
nodes.desc: menuPass is a threat group that has been active since at least 2006.

nodes.name: FIN7
nodes.desc: FIN7 is a financially-motivated threat group that has been active since 2013.

nodes.name: Gamaredon Group
nodes.desc: Gamaredon Group is a suspected Russian cyber espionage group that has targeted military, law enforcement, judiciary, non-profit, and non-governmental organizations in Ukraine since at least 2013.

nodes.name: RTM
nodes.desc: RTM is a cybercriminal group that has been active since at least 2015 and is primarily interested in users of remote banking systems in Russia and neighboring countries.

nodes.name: OilRig
nodes.aliases: COBALT GYPSY;IRN2;APT34;Helix Kitten;Evasive Serpens;Hazel Sandstorm;EUROPIUM;ITG13;Earth Simnavaz;Crambus;TA452
nodes.desc: OilRig is a suspected Iranian threat group that has targeted Middle Eastern and international victims since at least 2014.

nodes.name: APT32
nodes.desc: APT32 is a suspected Vietnam-based threat group that has been active since at least 2014.

nodes.name: FIN10
nodes.desc: FIN10 is a financially motivated threat group that has targeted organizations in North America since at least 2013 through 2016.

nodes.name: CopyKittens
nodes.desc: CopyKittens is an Iranian cyber espionage group that has been operating since at least 2013.

nodes.name: FIN5
nodes.desc: FIN5 is a financially motivated threat group that has targeted personally identifiable information and payment card information.

nodes.name: Sowbug
nodes.desc: Sowbug is a threat group that has conducted targeted attacks against organizations in South America and Southeast Asia, particularly government entities, since at least 2015.

nodes.name: PROMETHIUM
nodes.desc: PROMETHIUM is an activity group focused on espionage that has been active since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Magic Hound
nodes.desc: Magic Hound is an Iranian-sponsored threat group that conducts long term, resource-intensive cyber espionage operations, likely on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

nodes.name: BRONZE BUTLER
nodes.desc: BRONZE BUTLER is a cyber espionage group with likely Chinese origins that has been active since at least 2008.

nodes.name: FIN8
nodes.desc: FIN8 is a financially motivated threat group that has been active since at least January 2016, and known for targeting organizations in the hospitality, retail, entertainment, insurance, technology, chemical, and financial sectors.

nodes.name: TA459
nodes.desc: TA459 is a threat group believed to operate out of China that has targeted countries including Russia, Belarus, Mongolia, and others.

nodes.name: BlackOasis
nodes.desc: BlackOasis is a Middle Eastern threat group that is believed to be a customer of Gamma Group.

nodes.name: APT33
nodes.desc: APT33 is a suspected Iranian threat group that has carried out operations since at least 2013.

nodes.name: Leviathan
nodes.desc: Leviathan is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group that has been attributed to the Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Hainan State Security Department and an affiliated front company.

nodes.name: Elderwood
nodes.desc: Elderwood is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that was reportedly responsible for the 2009 Google intrusion known as Operation Aurora.

nodes.name: APT37
nodes.desc: APT37 is a North Korean state-sponsored cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2012.

nodes.name: PLATINUM
nodes.desc: PLATINUM is an activity group that has targeted victims since at least 2009.

nodes.name: MuddyWater
nodes.desc: MuddyWater is a cyber espionage group assessed to be a subordinate element within Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

nodes.name: Dark Caracal
nodes.desc: Dark Caracal is threat group that has been attributed to the Lebanese General Directorate of General Security (GDGS) and has operated since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Orangeworm
nodes.desc: Orangeworm is a group that has targeted organizations in the healthcare sector in the United States, Europe, and Asia since at least 2015, likely for the purpose of corporate espionage.

nodes.name: APT19
nodes.desc: APT19 is a Chinese-based threat group that has targeted a variety of industries, including defense, finance, energy, pharmaceutical, telecommunications, high tech, education, manufacturing, and legal services.

nodes.name: Rancor
nodes.desc: Rancor is a threat group that has led targeted campaigns against the South East Asia region.

nodes.name: Thrip
nodes.desc: Thrip is an espionage group that has targeted satellite communications, telecoms, and defense contractor companies in the U.S.

nodes.name: Leafminer
nodes.desc: Leafminer is an Iranian threat group that has targeted government organizations and business entities in the Middle East since at least early 2017.

nodes.name: Gorgon Group
nodes.desc: Gorgon Group is a threat group consisting of members who are suspected to be Pakistan-based or have other connections to Pakistan.

nodes.name: DarkHydrus
nodes.desc: DarkHydrus is a threat group that has targeted government agencies and educational institutions in the Middle East since at least 2016.

nodes.name: Cobalt Group
nodes.desc: Cobalt Group is a financially motivated threat group that has primarily targeted financial institutions since at least 2016.

nodes.name: Tropic Trooper
nodes.desc: Tropic Trooper is an unaffiliated threat group that has led targeted campaigns against targets in Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong.

nodes.name: APT38
nodes.desc: APT38 is a North Korean state-sponsored threat group that specializes in financial cyber operations; it has been attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau.

nodes.name: SilverTerrier
nodes.desc: SilverTerrier is a Nigerian threat group that has been seen active since 2014.

nodes.name: Gallmaker
nodes.desc: Gallmaker is a cyberespionage group that has targeted victims in the Middle East and has been active since at least December 2017.

nodes.name: FIN4
nodes.desc: FIN4 is a financially-motivated threat group that has targeted confidential information related to the public financial market, particularly regarding healthcare and pharmaceutical companies, since at least 2013.

nodes.name: APT39
nodes.desc: APT39 is one of several names for cyber espionage activity conducted by the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) through the front company Rana Intelligence Computing since at least 2014.

nodes.name: The White Company
nodes.desc: The White Company is a likely state-sponsored threat actor with advanced capabilities.

nodes.name: WIRTE
nodes.desc: WIRTE is a cyberespionage actor, believed to be a subgroup of the Hamas-affiliated Gaza Cybergang, that has been active since at least August 2018.

nodes.name: Silence
nodes.desc: Silence is a financially motivated threat actor targeting financial institutions in different countries.

nodes.name: TA505
nodes.desc: TA505 is a cyber criminal group that has been active since at least 2014.

nodes.name: GALLIUM
nodes.desc: GALLIUM is a cyberespionage group that has been active since at least 2012, primarily targeting telecommunications companies, financial institutions, and government entities in Afghanistan, Australia, Belgium, Cambodia, Malaysia, Mozambique, the Philippines, Russia, and Vietnam.

nodes.name: Kimsuky
nodes.desc: Kimsuky is a Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK)-based cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Machete
nodes.desc: Machete is a suspected Spanish-speaking cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2010.

nodes.name: APT41
nodes.desc: APT41 is a threat group that researchers have assessed as Chinese state-sponsored espionage group that also conducts financially-motivated operations.

nodes.name: BlackTech
nodes.desc: BlackTech is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that has primarily targeted organizations in East Asia--particularly Taiwan, Japan, and Hong Kong--and the US since at least 2013.

nodes.name: APT-C-36
nodes.desc: APT-C-36 is a suspected South American threat group that has engaged in espionage and financially motivated operations since at least 2018.

nodes.name: Inception
nodes.desc: Inception is a cyber espionage group active since at least 2014.

nodes.name: Wizard Spider
nodes.desc: Wizard Spider is a Russia-based financially motivated threat group originally known for the creation and deployment of TrickBot since at least 2016.

nodes.name: Mofang
nodes.desc: Mofang is a likely China-based cyber espionage group, named for its frequent practice of imitating a victim's infrastructure.

nodes.name: DarkVishnya
nodes.desc: DarkVishnya is a financially motivated threat actor targeting financial institutions in Eastern Europe.

nodes.name: Rocke
nodes.desc: Rocke is an alleged Chinese-speaking adversary whose primary objective appeared to be cryptojacking, or stealing victim system resources for the purposes of mining cryptocurrency.

nodes.name: Whitefly
nodes.desc: Whitefly is a cyber espionage group that has been operating since at least 2017.

nodes.name: Blue Mockingbird
nodes.desc: Blue Mockingbird is a cluster of observed activity involving Monero cryptocurrency-mining payloads in dynamic-link library (DLL) form on Windows systems.

nodes.name: Windshift
nodes.desc: Windshift is a threat group that has been active since at least 2017, targeting specific individuals for surveillance in government departments and critical infrastructure across the Middle East.

nodes.name: Chimera
nodes.desc: Chimera is a suspected China-based threat group that has been active since at least 2018 targeting the semiconductor industry in Taiwan as well as data from the airline industry.

nodes.name: GOLD SOUTHFIELD
nodes.desc: GOLD SOUTHFIELD is a financially motivated threat group active since at least 2018 that operates the REvil Ransomware-as-a Service (RaaS).

nodes.name: Fox Kitten
nodes.desc: Fox Kitten is threat actor with a suspected nexus to the Iranian government that has been active since at least 2017 against entities in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia, and North America.

nodes.name: Indrik Spider
nodes.desc: Indrik Spider is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since at least 2014.

nodes.name: Evilnum
nodes.desc: Evilnum is a financially motivated threat group that has been active since at least 2018.

nodes.name: Sidewinder
nodes.desc: Sidewinder is a suspected Indian threat actor group that has been active since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Silent Librarian
nodes.desc: Silent Librarian is a group that has targeted research and proprietary data at universities, government agencies, and private sector companies worldwide since at least 2013.

nodes.name: Volatile Cedar
nodes.desc: Volatile Cedar is a Lebanese threat group that has targeted individuals, companies, and institutions worldwide.

nodes.name: Windigo
nodes.desc: The Windigo group has been operating since at least 2011, compromising thousands of Linux and Unix servers using the Ebury SSH backdoor to create a spam botnet.

nodes.name: HAFNIUM
nodes.desc: HAFNIUM is a likely state-sponsored cyber espionage group operating out of China that has been active since at least January 2021.

nodes.name: Higaisa
nodes.desc: Higaisa is a threat group suspected to have South Korean origins.

nodes.name: TA551
nodes.desc: TA551 is a financially-motivated threat group that has been active since at least 2018.

nodes.name: ZIRCONIUM
nodes.desc: ZIRCONIUM is a threat group operating out of China, active since at least 2017, that has targeted individuals associated with the 2020 US presidential election and prominent leaders in the international affairs community.

nodes.name: Mustang Panda
nodes.aliases: TA416;RedDelta;BRONZE PRESIDENT;STATELY TAURUS;FIREANT;CAMARO DRAGON;EARTH PRETA;HIVE0154;TWILL TYPHOON;TANTALUM;LUMINOUS MOTH;UNC6384;TEMP.Hex;Red Lich;ClumsyToad
nodes.desc: Mustang Panda is a China-based cyber espionage threat actor that has been conducting operations since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Ajax Security Team
nodes.aliases: Operation Woolen-Goldfish;AjaxTM;Rocket Kitten;Flying Kitten;Operation Saffron Rose
nodes.desc: Ajax Security Team is a group that has been active since at least 2010 and believed to be operating out of Iran.

nodes.name: Tonto Team
nodes.desc: Tonto Team is a suspected Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage threat group that has primarily targeted South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and the United States since at least 2009; by 2020 they expanded operations to include other Asian as well as Eastern European countries.

nodes.name: Nomadic Octopus
nodes.desc: Nomadic Octopus is a Russian-speaking cyber espionage threat group that has primarily targeted Central Asia, including local governments, diplomatic missions, and individuals, since at least 2014.

nodes.name: Transparent Tribe
nodes.desc: Transparent Tribe is a suspected Pakistan-based threat group that has been active since at least 2013, primarily targeting diplomatic, defense, and research organizations in India and Afghanistan.

nodes.name: BackdoorDiplomacy
nodes.desc: BackdoorDiplomacy is a cyber espionage threat group that has been active since at least 2017.

nodes.name: IndigoZebra
nodes.desc: IndigoZebra is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group that has been targeting Central Asian governments since at least 2014.

nodes.name: Ferocious Kitten
nodes.desc: Ferocious Kitten is a threat group that has primarily targeted Persian-speaking individuals in Iran since at least 2015.

nodes.name: Andariel
nodes.desc: Andariel is a North Korean state-sponsored threat group that has been active since at least 2009.

nodes.name: TeamTNT
nodes.desc: TeamTNT is a threat group that has primarily targeted cloud and containerized environments.

nodes.name: LazyScripter
nodes.desc: LazyScripter is threat group that has mainly targeted the airlines industry since at least 2018, primarily using open-source toolsets.

nodes.name: Confucius
nodes.desc: Confucius is a cyber espionage group that has primarily targeted military personnel, high-profile personalities, business persons, and government organizations in South Asia since at least 2013.

nodes.name: Aquatic Panda
nodes.desc: Aquatic Panda is a suspected China-based threat group with a dual mission of intelligence collection and industrial espionage.

nodes.name: HEXANE
nodes.desc: HEXANE is a cyber espionage threat group that has targeted oil & gas, telecommunications, aviation, and internet service provider organizations since at least 2017.

nodes.name: BITTER
nodes.desc: BITTER is a suspected South Asian cyber espionage threat group that has been active since at least 2013.

nodes.name: Ember Bear
nodes.desc: Ember Bear is a Russian state-sponsored cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2020, linked to Russia's General Staff Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU) 161st Specialist Training Center (Unit 29155).

nodes.name: LAPSUS$
nodes.desc: LAPSUS$ is cyber criminal threat group that has been active since at least mid-2021.

nodes.name: POLONIUM
nodes.desc: POLONIUM is a Lebanon-based group that has primarily targeted Israeli organizations, including critical manufacturing, information technology, and defense industry companies, since at least February 2022.

nodes.name: Earth Lusca
nodes.desc: Earth Lusca is a suspected China-based cyber espionage group that has been active since at least April 2019.

nodes.name: Aoqin Dragon
nodes.desc: Aoqin Dragon is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage threat group that has been active since at least 2013.

nodes.name: SideCopy
nodes.desc: SideCopy is a Pakistani threat group that has primarily targeted South Asian countries, including Indian and Afghani government personnel, since at least 2019.

nodes.name: Moses Staff
nodes.desc: Moses Staff is a suspected Iranian threat group that has primarily targeted Israeli companies since at least September 2021.

nodes.name: EXOTIC LILY
nodes.desc: EXOTIC LILY is a financially motivated group that has been closely linked with Wizard Spider and the deployment of ransomware including Conti and Diavol.

nodes.name: CURIUM
nodes.desc: CURIUM is an Iranian threat group, first reported in September 2019 and active since at least July 2018, targeting IT service providers in the Middle East.

nodes.name: Metador
nodes.desc: Metador is a suspected cyber espionage group that was first reported in September 2022.

nodes.name: LuminousMoth
nodes.desc: LuminousMoth is a Chinese-speaking cyber espionage group that has been active since at least October 2020.

nodes.name: Scattered Spider
nodes.desc: Scattered Spider is a native English-speaking cybercriminal group active since at least 2022.

nodes.name: FIN13
nodes.desc: FIN13 is a financially motivated cyber threat group that has targeted the financial, retail, and hospitality industries in Mexico and Latin America, as early as 2016.

nodes.name: Volt Typhoon
nodes.desc: Volt Typhoon is a People's Republic of China (PRC) state-sponsored actor that has been active since at least 2021, primarily targeting critical infrastructure organizations in the US and its territories including Guam.

nodes.name: TA2541
nodes.desc: TA2541 is a cybercriminal group that has been targeting the aviation, aerospace, transportation, manufacturing, and defense industries since at least 2017.

nodes.name: MoustachedBouncer
nodes.desc: MoustachedBouncer is a cyberespionage group that has been active since at least 2014 targeting foreign embassies in Belarus.

nodes.name: Mustard Tempest
nodes.desc: Mustard Tempest is an initial access broker that has operated the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017.

nodes.name: Cinnamon Tempest
nodes.desc: Cinnamon Tempest is a China-based threat group that has been active since at least 2021 deploying multiple strains of ransomware based on the leaked Babuk source code.

nodes.name: ToddyCat
nodes.desc: ToddyCat is a sophisticated threat group that has been active since at least 2020 using custom loaders and malware in multi-stage infection chains against government and military targets across Europe and Asia.

nodes.name: APT5
nodes.desc: APT5 is a China-based espionage actor that has been active since at least 2007 primarily targeting the telecommunications, aerospace, and defense industries throughout the U.S., Europe, and Asia.

nodes.name: Akira
nodes.desc: Akira is a ransomware variant and ransomware deployment entity active since at least March 2023.

nodes.name: Malteiro
nodes.desc: Malteiro is a financially motivated criminal group that is likely based in Brazil and has been active since at least November 2019.

nodes.name: Agrius
nodes.desc: Agrius is an Iranian threat actor active since 2020 notable for a series of ransomware and wiper operations in the Middle East, with an emphasis on Israeli targets.

nodes.name: Saint Bear
nodes.desc: Saint Bear is a Russian-nexus threat actor active since early 2021, primarily targeting entities in Ukraine and Georgia.

nodes.name: INC Ransom
nodes.desc: INC Ransom is a ransomware and data extortion threat group associated with the deployment of INC Ransomware that has been active since at least July 2023.

nodes.name: Star Blizzard
nodes.desc: Star Blizzard is a cyber espionage and influence group originating in Russia that has been active since at least 2019.

nodes.name: Daggerfly
nodes.desc: Daggerfly is a People's Republic of China-linked APT entity active since at least 2012.

nodes.name: Winter Vivern
nodes.desc: Winter Vivern is a group linked to Russian and Belorussian interests active since at least 2020 targeting various European government and NGO entities, along with sporadic targeting of Indian and US victims.

nodes.name: Moonstone Sleet
nodes.desc: Moonstone Sleet is a North Korean-linked threat actor executing both financially motivated attacks and espionage operations.

nodes.name: TA577
nodes.desc: TA577 is an initial access broker (IAB) that has distributed QakBot and Pikabot, and was among the first observed groups distributing Latrodectus in 2023.

nodes.name: TA578
nodes.desc: TA578 is a threat actor that has used contact forms and email to initiate communications with victims and to distribute malware including Latrodectus, IcedID, and Bumblebee.

nodes.name: RedCurl
nodes.desc: RedCurl is a threat actor active since 2018 notable for corporate espionage targeting a variety of locations, including Ukraine, Canada and the United Kingdom, and a variety of industries, including but not limited to travel agencies, insurance companies, and banks.

nodes.name: Play
nodes.desc: Play is a ransomware group that has been active since at least 2022 deploying  Playcrypt ransomware against the business, government, critical infrastructure, healthcare, and media sectors in North America, South America, and Europe.

nodes.name: Sea Turtle
nodes.desc: Sea Turtle is a Türkiye-linked threat actor active since at least 2017 performing espionage and service provider compromise operations against victims in Asia, Europe, and North America.

nodes.name: RedEcho
nodes.desc: RedEcho is a People’s Republic of China-related threat actor associated with long-running intrusions in Indian critical infrastructure entities.

nodes.name: BlackByte
nodes.desc: BlackByte is a ransomware threat actor operating since at least 2021.

nodes.name: APT42
nodes.desc: APT42 is an Iranian-sponsored threat group that conducts cyber espionage and surveillance.

nodes.name: Salt Typhoon
nodes.desc: Salt Typhoon is a People's Republic of China (PRC) state-backed actor that has been active since at least 2019 and responsible for numerous compromises of network infrastructure at major U.S.

nodes.name: Storm-1811
nodes.desc: Storm-1811 is a financially-motivated entity linked to Black Basta ransomware deployment.

nodes.name: Velvet Ant
nodes.desc: Velvet Ant is a threat actor operating since at least 2021.

nodes.name: UNC3886
nodes.desc: UNC3886 is a China-nexus cyberespionage group that has been active since at least 2022, targeting defense, technology, and telecommunication organizations located in the United States and the Asia-Pacific-Japan (APJ) regions.

nodes.name: AppleJeus
nodes.desc: AppleJeus is a North Korean state-sponsored threat group attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau.

nodes.name: Water Galura
nodes.desc: Water Galura are the operators of the Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) who handle payload generation, ransom negotiations, and the publication of stolen data for Qilin affilates recruited on Russian cybercrime forums.

nodes.name: Medusa Group
nodes.desc: Medusa Group has been active since at least 2021 and was initially operated as a closed ransomware group before evolving into a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation.

nodes.name: Contagious Interview
nodes.desc: Contagious Interview is a North Korea–aligned threat group active since 2023.

nodes.name: Storm-0501
nodes.desc: Storm-0501 is a financially motivated cyber criminal group that uses commodity and open-source tools to conduct ransomware operations.

nodes.name: MirrorFace
nodes.desc: MirrorFace is a People's Republic of China (PRC)-aligned cyberespionage actor believed to be a subgroup under the menuPass umbrella based on targeting, tools, and infrastructure overlaps.

nodes.name: VOID MANTICORE
nodes.aliases: COBALT MYSTIQUE;Handala Hack;Homeland Justice;Karma;Karmabelow80;BANISHED KITTEN;Red Sandstorm
nodes.desc: VOID MANTICORE is a threat group assessed to operate on behalf of Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

nodes.name: TeamPCP
nodes.desc: TeamPCP is a financially-motivated, cloud-native threat group that has been active since at least September 2025.

nodes.name: ShinyHunters
nodes.desc: ShinyHunters is a cyber criminal collective that has been active since at least 2019 operating under the ShinyCorp persona.

nodes.name: The Gentlemen
nodes.desc: The Gentlemen is a group that maintains the The Gentlemen Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS).

nodes.name: NIMBUS MANTICORE
nodes.desc: NIMBUS MANTICORE is a State Sponsored cyber espionage group associated with the Iranian Regime specifically the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

nodes.name: Data Obfuscation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obfuscate command and control traffic to make it more difficult to detect.

nodes.name: Junk Data
nodes.desc: Adversaries may add junk data to protocols used for command and control to make detection more difficult.

nodes.name: Steganography
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use steganographic techniques to hide command and control traffic to make detection efforts more difficult.

nodes.name: Protocol or Service Impersonation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may impersonate legitimate protocols or web service traffic to disguise command and control activity and thwart analysis efforts.

nodes.name: OS Credential Dumping
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password.

nodes.name: LSASS Memory
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS).

nodes.name: Security Account Manager
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to extract credential material from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database either through in-memory techniques or through the Windows Registry where the SAM database is stored.

nodes.name: NTDS
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to access or create a copy of the Active Directory domain database in order to steal credential information, as well as obtain other information about domain members such as devices, users, and access rights.

nodes.name: LSA Secrets
nodes.desc: Adversaries with SYSTEM access to a host may attempt to access Local Security Authority (LSA) secrets, which can contain a variety of different credential materials, such as credentials for service accounts.

nodes.name: Cached Domain Credentials
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to access cached domain credentials used to allow authentication to occur in the event a domain controller is unavailable.

nodes.name: DCSync
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to access credentials and other sensitive information by abusing a Windows Domain Controller's application programming interface (API)    to simulate the replication process from a remote domain controller using a technique called DCSync.

nodes.name: Data from Local System
nodes.desc: Adversaries may search local system sources, such as file systems, configuration files, local databases, virtual machine files, or process memory, to find files of interest and sensitive data prior to Exfiltration.

nodes.name: Direct Volume Access
nodes.desc: Adversaries may directly access a volume to bypass file access controls and file system monitoring.

nodes.name: System Service Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may try to gather information about registered local system services.

nodes.name: Fallback Channels
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use fallback or alternate communication channels if the primary channel is compromised or inaccessible in order to maintain reliable command and control and to avoid data transfer thresholds.

nodes.name: Application Window Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of open application windows.

nodes.name: Query Registry
nodes.desc: Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry to gather information about the system, configuration, and installed software.

nodes.name: Rootkit
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use rootkits to hide the presence of programs, files, network connections, services, drivers, and other system components.

nodes.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings, such as IP and/or MAC addresses, of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems.

nodes.name: Internet Connection Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may check for Internet connectivity on compromised systems.

nodes.name: Wi-Fi Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may search for information about Wi-Fi networks, such as network names and passwords, on compromised systems.

nodes.name: Remote System Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system.

nodes.name: Automated Exfiltration
nodes.desc: Adversaries may exfiltrate data, such as sensitive documents, through the use of automated processing after being gathered during Collection.

nodes.name: Traffic Duplication
nodes.desc: Adversaries may leverage traffic mirroring in order to automate data exfiltration over compromised infrastructure.

nodes.name: Remote Services
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service that accepts remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and VNC.

nodes.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

nodes.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with a remote network share using Server Message Block (SMB).

nodes.name: SSH
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote machines using Secure Shell (SSH).

nodes.name: VNC
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to remotely control machines using Virtual Network Computing (VNC).

nodes.name: Windows Remote Management
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with remote systems using Windows Remote Management (WinRM).

nodes.name: Cloud Services
nodes.desc: Adversaries may log into accessible cloud services within a compromised environment using Valid Accounts that are synchronized with or federated to on-premises user identities.

nodes.name: Data from Removable Media
nodes.desc: Adversaries may search connected removable media on computers they have compromised to find files of interest.

nodes.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit.

nodes.name: Binary Padding
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use binary padding to add junk data and change the on-disk representation of malware.

nodes.name: Software Packing
nodes.desc: Adversaries may perform software packing or virtual machine software protection to conceal their code.

nodes.name: Steganography
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use steganography techniques in order to prevent the detection of hidden information.

nodes.name: Compile After Delivery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to make payloads difficult to discover and analyze by delivering files to victims as uncompiled code.

nodes.name: Indicator Removal from Tools
nodes.desc: Adversaries may remove indicators from tools if they believe their malicious tool was detected, quarantined, or otherwise curtailed.

nodes.name: HTML Smuggling
nodes.desc: Adversaries may smuggle data and files past content filters by hiding malicious payloads inside of seemingly benign HTML files.

nodes.name: Dynamic API Resolution
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obfuscate then dynamically resolve API functions called by their malware in order to conceal malicious functionalities and impair defensive analysis.

nodes.name: Embedded Payloads
nodes.desc: Adversaries may embed payloads within other files to conceal malicious content from defenses.

nodes.name: Command Obfuscation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obfuscate content during command execution to impede detection.

nodes.name: Fileless Storage
nodes.desc: Adversaries may store data in "fileless" formats to conceal malicious activity from defenses.

nodes.name: LNK Icon Smuggling
nodes.desc: Adversaries may smuggle commands to download malicious payloads past content filters by hiding them within otherwise seemingly benign windows shortcut files.

nodes.name: Encrypted/Encoded File
nodes.desc: Adversaries may encrypt or encode files to obfuscate strings, bytes, and other specific patterns to impede detection.

nodes.name: Compression
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use compression to obfuscate their payloads or files.

nodes.name: Junk Code Insertion
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use junk code / dead code to obfuscate a malware’s functionality.

nodes.name: Scheduled Transfer
nodes.desc: Adversaries may schedule data exfiltration to be performed only at certain times of day or at certain intervals.

nodes.name: Data Transfer Size Limits
nodes.desc: An adversary may exfiltrate data in fixed size chunks instead of whole files or limit packet sizes below certain thresholds.

nodes.name: System Owner/User Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to identify the primary user, currently logged in user, set of users that commonly uses a system, or whether a user is actively using the system.

nodes.name: Masquerading
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate or benign to users and/or security tools.

nodes.name: Invalid Code Signature
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to mimic features of valid code signatures to increase the chance of deceiving a user, analyst, or tool.

nodes.name: Right-to-Left Override
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse the right-to-left override (RTLO or RLO) character (U+202E) to disguise a string and/or file name to make it appear benign.

nodes.name: Rename Legitimate Utilities
nodes.desc: Adversaries may rename legitimate / system utilities to try to evade security mechanisms concerning the usage of those utilities.

nodes.name: Masquerade Task or Service
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate the name of a task or service to make it appear legitimate or benign.

nodes.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
nodes.desc: Adversaries may match or approximate the name or location of legitimate files, Registry keys, or other resources when naming/placing them.

nodes.name: Space after Filename
nodes.desc: Adversaries can hide a program's true filetype by changing the extension of a file.

nodes.name: Double File Extension
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse a double extension in the filename as a means of masquerading the true file type.

nodes.name: Masquerade File Type
nodes.desc: Adversaries may masquerade malicious payloads as legitimate files through changes to the payload's formatting, including the file’s signature, extension, icon, and contents.

nodes.name: Masquerade Account Name
nodes.desc: Adversaries may match or approximate the names of legitimate accounts to make newly created ones appear benign.

nodes.name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use scripts automatically executed at boot or logon initialization to establish persistence.

nodes.name: Logon Script (Windows)
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Windows logon scripts automatically executed at logon initialization to establish persistence.

nodes.name: RC Scripts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may establish persistence by modifying RC scripts, which are executed during a Unix-like system’s startup.

nodes.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
nodes.desc: Adversaries may search network shares on computers they have compromised to find files of interest.

nodes.name: Network Sniffing
nodes.desc: Adversaries may passively sniff network traffic to capture information about an environment, including authentication material passed over the network.

nodes.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
nodes.desc: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

nodes.name: Network Service Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation.

nodes.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious commands and payloads.

nodes.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing command and control channel.

nodes.name: Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an asymmetrically encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel.

nodes.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an un-encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel.

nodes.name: System Network Connections Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.

nodes.name: Exfiltration over USB
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to exfiltrate data over a USB connected physical device.

nodes.name: At
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse the at utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.

nodes.name: Cron
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse the cron utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.

nodes.name: Scheduled Task
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.

nodes.name: Systemd Timers
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse systemd timers to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code.

nodes.name: Process Injection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Dynamic-link Library Injection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Portable Executable Injection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject portable executables (PE) into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Asynchronous Procedure Call
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject malicious code into processes via the asynchronous procedure call (APC) queue in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Process Hollowing
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject malicious code into suspended and hollowed processes in order to evade process-based defenses.

nodes.name: Process Doppelgänging
nodes.desc: Adversaries may inject malicious code into process via process doppelgänging in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Input Capture
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or collect information.

nodes.name: Keylogging
nodes.desc: Adversaries may log user keystrokes to intercept credentials as the user types them.

nodes.name: GUI Input Capture
nodes.desc: Adversaries may mimic common operating system GUI components to prompt users for credentials with a seemingly legitimate prompt.

nodes.name: Web Portal Capture
nodes.desc: Adversaries may install code on externally facing portals, such as a VPN login page, to capture and transmit credentials of users who attempt to log into the service.

nodes.name: Credential API Hooking
nodes.desc: Adversaries may hook into Windows application programming interface (API) functions and Linux system functions to collect user credentials.

nodes.name: Process Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get information about running processes on a system.

nodes.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

nodes.name: PowerShell
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

nodes.name: AppleScript
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse AppleScript for execution.

nodes.name: Windows Command Shell
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.

nodes.name: Unix Shell
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

nodes.name: Visual Basic
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VB) for execution.

nodes.name: Python
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse Python commands and scripts for execution.

nodes.name: JavaScript
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse various implementations of JavaScript for execution.

nodes.name: Network Device CLI
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse scripting or built-in command line interpreters (CLI) on network devices to execute malicious command and payloads.

nodes.name: Cloud API
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse cloud APIs to execute malicious commands.

nodes.name: AutoHotKey & AutoIT
nodes.desc: Adversaries may execute commands and perform malicious tasks using AutoIT and AutoHotKey automation scripts.

nodes.name: Hypervisor CLI
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse hypervisor command line interpreters (CLIs) to execute malicious commands.

nodes.name: Container CLI/API
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse built-in CLI tools or API calls to execute malicious commands in containerized environments.

nodes.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.

nodes.name: Permission Groups Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to discover group and permission settings.

nodes.name: Local Groups
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to find local system groups and permission settings.

nodes.name: Domain Groups
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to find domain-level groups and permission settings.

nodes.name: Cloud Groups
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to find cloud groups and permission settings.

nodes.name: Indicator Removal
nodes.desc: Adversaries may selectively delete or modify artifacts generated to reduce indications of their presence and blend in with legitimate activity.

nodes.name: Clear Command History
nodes.desc: In addition to clearing system logs, an adversary may clear the command history of a compromised account to conceal the actions undertaken during an intrusion.

nodes.name: File Deletion
nodes.desc: Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.

nodes.name: Network Share Connection Removal
nodes.desc: Adversaries may remove share connections that are no longer useful in order to clean up traces of their operation.

nodes.name: Timestomp
nodes.desc: Adversaries may modify file time attributes to hide new files or changes to existing files.

nodes.name: Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
nodes.desc: Adversaries may clear or remove evidence of malicious network connections in order to clean up traces of their operations.

nodes.name: Clear Mailbox Data
nodes.desc: Adversaries may modify mail and mail application data to remove evidence of their activity.

nodes.name: Clear Persistence
nodes.desc: Adversaries may clear artifacts associated with previously established persistence on a host system to remove evidence of their activity.

nodes.name: Application Layer Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

nodes.name: Web Protocols
nodes.desc: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

nodes.name: File Transfer Protocols
nodes.desc: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with transferring files to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

nodes.name: Mail Protocols
nodes.desc: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with electronic mail delivery to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

nodes.name: DNS
nodes.desc: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) application layer protocol to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

nodes.name: Software Deployment Tools
nodes.desc: Adversaries may gain access to and use centralized software suites installed within an enterprise to execute commands and move laterally through the network.

nodes.name: Data Staged
nodes.desc: Adversaries may stage collected data in a central location or directory prior to Exfiltration.

nodes.name: Local Data Staging
nodes.desc: Adversaries may stage collected data in a central location or directory on the local system prior to Exfiltration.

nodes.name: Remote Data Staging
nodes.desc: Adversaries may stage data collected from multiple systems in a central location or directory on one system prior to Exfiltration.

nodes.name: Valid Accounts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

nodes.name: Default Accounts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a default account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

nodes.name: Domain Accounts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a domain account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

nodes.name: Local Accounts
nodes.desc: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

nodes.name: Cloud Accounts
nodes.desc: Valid accounts in cloud environments may allow adversaries to perform actions to achieve Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

nodes.name: Taint Shared Content
nodes.desc: Adversaries may deliver payloads to remote systems by adding content to shared storage locations, such as network drives or internal code repositories.

nodes.name: System Information Discovery
nodes.desc: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, hotfixes, service packs, and architecture.

nodes.name: File and Directory Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or may search in specific locations of a host or network share for certain information within a file system.

nodes.name: Account Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment.

nodes.name: Local Account
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts.

nodes.name: Domain Account
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.

nodes.name: Email Account
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of email addresses and accounts.

nodes.name: Cloud Account
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of cloud accounts.

nodes.name: Proxy
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications to a command and control server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure.

nodes.name: Internal Proxy
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an internal proxy to direct command and control traffic between two or more systems in a compromised environment.

nodes.name: External Proxy
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an external proxy to act as an intermediary for network communications to a command and control server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure.

nodes.name: Multi-hop Proxy
nodes.desc: Adversaries may chain together multiple proxies to disguise the source of malicious traffic.

nodes.name: Domain Fronting
nodes.desc: Adversaries may take advantage of routing schemes in Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) and other services which host multiple domains to obfuscate the intended destination of HTTPS traffic or traffic tunneled through HTTPS.

nodes.name: Replication Through Removable Media
nodes.desc: Adversaries may move onto systems, possibly those on disconnected or air-gapped networks, by copying malware to removable media and taking advantage of Autorun features when the media is inserted into a system and executes.

nodes.name: Communication Through Removable Media
nodes.desc: Adversaries can perform command and control between compromised hosts on potentially disconnected networks using removable media to transfer commands from system to system.

nodes.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an OSI non-application layer protocol for communication between host and C2 server or among infected hosts within a network.

nodes.name: Account Manipulation
nodes.desc: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain and/or elevate access to victim systems.

nodes.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
nodes.desc: Adversaries may add adversary-controlled credentials to a cloud account to maintain persistent access to victim accounts and instances within the environment.

nodes.name: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
nodes.desc: Adversaries may grant additional permission levels to maintain persistent access to an adversary-controlled email account.

nodes.name: Additional Cloud Roles
nodes.desc: An adversary may add additional roles or permissions to an adversary-controlled cloud account to maintain persistent access to a tenant.

nodes.name: SSH Authorized Keys
nodes.desc: Adversaries may modify the SSH authorized_keys file to maintain persistence on a victim host.

nodes.name: Device Registration
nodes.desc: Adversaries may register a device to an adversary-controlled account.

nodes.name: Additional Local or Domain Groups
nodes.desc: An adversary may add additional local or domain groups to an adversary-controlled account to maintain persistent access to a system or domain.

nodes.name: Web Service
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for relaying data to/from a compromised system.

nodes.name: Dead Drop Resolver
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service to host information that points to additional command and control (C2) infrastructure.

nodes.name: Bidirectional Communication
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to and receiving output from a compromised system over the Web service channel.

nodes.name: One-Way Communication
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to a compromised system without receiving return output over the Web service channel.

nodes.name: Multi-Stage Channels
nodes.desc: Adversaries may create multiple stages for command and control that are employed under different conditions or for certain functions.

nodes.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
nodes.desc: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

nodes.name: Native API
nodes.desc: Adversaries may interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to execute behaviors.

nodes.name: Brute Force
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.

nodes.name: Password Guessing
nodes.desc: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials within the system or environment may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts.

nodes.name: Password Cracking
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use password cracking to attempt to recover usable credentials, such as plaintext passwords, when credential material such as password hashes are obtained.

nodes.name: Password Spraying
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.

nodes.name: Credential Stuffing
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from breach dumps of unrelated accounts to gain access to target accounts through credential overlap.

nodes.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
nodes.desc: Adversaries may target multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms, (i.e., smart cards, token generators, etc.) to gain access to credentials that can be used to access systems, services, and network resources.

nodes.name: Modify Registry
nodes.desc: Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry as part of a variety of other techniques to aid in defense evasion, persistence, and execution.

nodes.name: Screen Capture
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to take screen captures of the desktop to gather information over the course of an operation.

nodes.name: Email Collection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may target user email to collect sensitive information.

nodes.name: Local Email Collection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may target user email on local systems to collect sensitive information.

nodes.name: Remote Email Collection
nodes.desc: Adversaries may target an Exchange server, Office 365, or Google Workspace to collect sensitive information.

nodes.name: Email Forwarding Rule
nodes.desc: Adversaries may setup email forwarding rules to collect sensitive information.

nodes.name: Clipboard Data
nodes.desc: Adversaries may collect data stored in the clipboard from users copying information within or between applications.

nodes.name: Automated Collection
nodes.desc: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.

nodes.name: Peripheral Device Discovery
nodes.desc: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about attached peripheral devices and components connected to a computer system.

nodes.name: Audio Capture
nodes.desc: An adversary can leverage a computer's peripheral devices (e.g., microphones and webcams) or applications (e.g., voice and video call services) to capture audio recordings for the purpose of listening into sensitive conversations to gather information.

nodes.name: System Time Discovery
nodes.desc: An adversary may gather the system time and/or time zone settings from a local or remote system.

nodes.name: Video Capture
nodes.desc: An adversary can leverage a computer's peripheral devices (e.g., integrated cameras or webcams) or applications (e.g., video call services) to capture video recordings for the purpose of gathering information.

nodes.name: Shared Modules
nodes.desc: Adversaries may execute malicious payloads via loading shared modules.

nodes.name: Standard Encoding
nodes.desc: Adversaries may encode data with a standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect.

nodes.name: Non-Standard Encoding
nodes.desc: Adversaries may encode data with a non-standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect.

nodes.name: External Remote Services
nodes.desc: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network.

nodes.name: Access Token Manipulation

nodes.name: Make and Impersonate Token

nodes.name: Domain Account

nodes.name: Cloud Account
nodes.desc: Adversaries may create a cloud account to maintain access to victim systems.

nodes.name: Outlook Home Page
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook's Home Page feature to obtain persistence on a compromised system.

nodes.name: Add-ins

nodes.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
nodes.desc: Adversaries may use Obfuscated Files or Information to hide artifacts of an intrusion from analysis.

nodes.name: Browser Extensions

nodes.name: IDE Extensions
nodes.desc: Adversaries may abuse an integrated development environment (IDE) extension to establish persistent access to victim systems.

nodes.name: Browser Session Hijacking
nodes.desc: Adversaries may take advantage of security vulnerabilities and inherent functionality in browser software to change content, modify user-behaviors, and intercept information as part of various browser session hijacking techniques.
